Targets and simulations are not achieved database performance

This assessment analytically represents the full population and simulates 17,280,000 foreground requests plus 2,218,221 background events. It does not load a 100M-row CockroachDB database. A small actual OPA HTTP microbenchmark is reported separately.

Reserve capacity; do not buy directly from synthetic slot counts

Peak demand is around 88% of the initial assumed DB capacity. A 25% workload increase overloads it. A 50% increase in effective capacity lowers peak demand to about 59%, providing a useful AZ-loss reserve. Effective queue slots are not CPUs. Measure the actual limiting resource, then tune or scale the physical deployment.

Scale changes the integration design

PoC behaviorPilot/scale changeReason

Replace entire projection graphVersioned deltas with atomic parent closure and manifest/inbox updateAvoid repeated indexes, payload and WAN amplification.

Check remote home authority on every readStrict WAN budget OR approved bounded local authority leaseLow local latency and immediate cross-WAN consistency are different contracts.
One poller / raw UI snapshotPartitioned regional relay, priority revocation, materialized aggregatesBound queue age, retry storms and monitor load.

Remote authority needs a deliberate contract

The illustrative synchronous WAN case adds a 180ms median round trip and takes relationship p99 to roughly 309ms. A local-read target requires local facts and an approved freshness contract. The proposed alternative uses resource/scope/table epochs plus a maximum five-second authority lease inclusive of clock tolerance. A partition lease must bind a contiguous applied revocation watermark: a heartbeat alone cannot prove no revocation was missed. Refresh active partitions in batches, not every one of 100M scopes every five seconds. This is a proposed pilot design requiring approval; the current PoC still consults source authority.

Priority revocation traffic must stay separate from data backfill. A 30-minute UK receiver outage generates about 4.97M pending jobs in the model. At 1.5× incoming-rate service capacity, recovery takes 60 minutes while new traffic continues. If the destination remains unavailable, show purge pending; do not promise completed deletion.

Method and limits

Sixteen scenarios × three seeds; 360,000 foreground arrivals per run and separate import arrivals. At design peak each run covers roughly ten seconds. This is a finite event model; overload results are growing queues, not steady-state percentiles. Service times, cache misses, retry rates and effective concurrency are assumed. The p99 range across seeds describes random variation, not calibration confidence. Lower population points reuse the same full-scale model capacity and proportionately lower traffic. Real SQL, disk, compaction, fault and long-soak tests remain necessary.

Targets apply by operation/cell/entity to bounded responses, alongside timeout and error rates. Count dropped load-generator iterations and censored timeouts; do not report successful-only percentiles. The actual OPA microbenchmark measured sequential loopback HTTP only and is not a system throughput benchmark.

For implementers: engineering brief
HAND OFF TO ENGINEERING

Build this component

A focused prompt with scope, contracts and acceptance criteria.

Read the full prompt
Operational isolation decision: use three regional work classes: authority guard, operational delivery and bulk reconciliation. Separate relay paths, queues/topics, worker groups, connection/concurrency budgets and retry/quarantine paths. A policy transaction advances scoped authority and creates a guard intent plus one reconciliation cursor; it must not enumerate affected rows. Operational commits remain local ACID with outbox/audit/idempotency. Operational priority never bypasses current policy. Source restriction commit, remote enforcement and physical convergence are separate milestones. Read the Work isolation page before implementing any queue or policy change. The interactive lab and admission specification are synthetic; the v3 database harness still has its original process lock and serial worker.

Use the published capacity model as an explicit hypothesis, never as a database benchmark. Target 50M parties, 100M relationships and the supplied typed child-table distribution. Normal workload is 10k reads/s + 1k writes/s; design peak is 30k reads/s + 5k writes/s globally. Preserve geography, entitlement, purpose and explicit-deny semantics. Use the scale/ scripts and measured workload aggregates to replace assumptions. The v3 runtime remains a PoC with full scans and a process lock; no optimized production data path has been implemented.

Build the pilot benchmark, not a benchmark-shaped demo. Generate full indexed child-table cardinality with reproducible degree and policy skew. Use an open arrival model; 60-minute design-peak test and 24-hour normal soak. Report p95/p99/p99.9 per operation and region, errors, dropped iterations, DB resource use, retries, oldest revocation and destination freshness. Replace assumed queue capacity with observations before recommending hardware. Test hot keys, cold caches, background compaction, backup and an AZ loss.
